review_candidates.title: Principal, Sustainable Energies & Infrastructure Credit
review_candidates.description: Purpose. Performance. People. Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians. With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide. For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success. The Role As a Principal, Sustainable Energies & Infrastructure Credit (“SEIC”), you will play a leadership role in originating, underwriting, executing, and managing credit investments across the energy and infrastructure sectors, with a primary geographic focus on North America. The role will have accountability for transaction outcomes and portfolio performance, while contributing to the continued development of the Sustainable Energies & Infrastructure Credit strategy. Based in Toronto and reporting to a Managing Director, you will bring a proactive approach to origination, sound investment judgment, and a collaborative mindset. You will develop and manage relationships across the market, and lead and develop colleagues while contributing to the long-term success of the SEIC strategy. The Team Real Assets Credit (“RAC”) brings together CPP Investments’ expertise across real estate, infrastructure, and energy to invest in real asset credit opportunities globally. Managing approximately C$12 billion in assets, RAC seeks attractive risk-adjusted returns through proactive origination, rigorous fundamental analysis, and partnerships with experienced sponsors and co-lenders. Within RAC, the SEIC team invests flexibly across the capital structure, primarily in private, below-investment-grade credit investments. The team invests across infrastructure, renewable energy, and conventional energy end markets. Investments include senior and unitranche loans, mezzanine and holdco loans, preferred equity and structured equity with credit-like characteristics, and, selectively, broadly syndicated bonds and loans. Accountabilities Lead the analysis, underwriting, internal investment committee process, execution, and monitoring of SEIC credit investment opportunities, with accountability for investment and portfolio outcomes. Proactively originate investment opportunities and build enduring relationships with sponsors, management teams, financial institutions, advisors, and other market participants. Assess credit risk and determine appropriate pricing, structure, covenants, downside protections, and position sizing. Evaluate project economics, business models, capital structures, sponsor strength, market dynamics, and key downside risks across relevant energy and infrastructure sectors. Perform and manage detailed due diligence processes, including the selection, scoping, and oversight of third-party legal, technical, tax, accounting, insurance, and commercial advisors. Direct and oversee the development of detailed financial models, scenario analyses, debt-sizing analyses, liquidity assessments, and downside cases. Develop investment committee recommendations and play a major role in presenting investment conclusions, articulating key risks and mitigants, and responding to challenging technical questions. Contribute to building a high-performing investment team, fostering accountability, inclusion, collaboration, and talent development while building relationships across Real Assets Credit and CPP Investments. What You Bring A relevant undergraduate or advanced degree. A professional designation such as the CFA is an asset. Significant energy and/or infrastructure investment or credit experience, preferably with a focus on North America. 8+ years of relevant experience, ideally gained at an established investment manager or investment bank. A credit-led investment approach, strong judgment, and an ownership mindset. Experience originating, underwriting, structuring, and executing large-scale credit investments. Knowledge of project economics and risks, and business models, across a range of sub-sectors, including renewable power, firm power, infrastructure, digital infrastructure, and conventional energy. The ideal candidate will have experience across several verticals, with some specialization, rather than a focus on only one vertical. Experience working in deal teams and developing junior talent. Leading detailed due diligence processes and managing external advisors. Strong interpersonal and relationship building skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with colleagues, management teams, investment partners, and external advisors. You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment. We provide colleagues with cutting-edge AI tools, dedicated learning time, and practical support to help them deliver with greater impact. Inclusion & Accessibility CPP Investments is committed to equitable access to employment and building a workforce that reflects diverse talent and perspectives. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs. Attention: Protect Yourself from Fraud CPP Investments is committed to a secure and transparent recruitment process. We will never ask candidates for payment or financial information at any stage of hiring. All legitimate opportunities are posted on our careers page, and communications will come from our applicant tracking system, Workday. CPP Investments may use AI tools to help screen and assess applicants by analyzing resumes and applications for relevant skills and experience. These tools support, but do not replace, human decision-making.

review_candidates.title: Postdoctoral Researcher
review_candidates.description: Full job advertisment here: https://web103.reachmee.com/ext/I005/1015/job?site=7&lang=UK&validator=e5819a4704cd849685049472c0c17895&job_id=p4888 We are looking for a Postdoc in the research project GIVE RIGHTS and the subject of IMER (International Migration and Ethnic Relations) at the department of Global Political Studies, Faculty of Culture and Society. Subject area Scholars within IMER study, among other subjects, the national, regional, international, and global causes and effects of migration in both the society of origin and destination on a structural, institutional, collective, and individual level. IMER is an inherently multi- and interdisciplinary subject, in which sociology, political science, cultural geography, anthropology, economic history, economics, social work, history, ethnology, religious studies, gender studies, and cultural studies are represented. Job description As a postdoc at Malmö University, you will be able to develop your independence as a researcher after completing your doctoral degree and enable additional qualifications. The position is primarily intended to allow attainment of research qualifications. Teaching may also be included in the duties, though only at most one-fifth of working hours. The position is also to provide the opportunity for educational qualifications and higher education teaching training. The position’s duties include research of at least 90 % and teaching of at most 10 % within IMER or other relevant subjects at GPS. The postdoc will be responsible for the Italian case study in the GIVE RIGHTS project. This includes conducting a media study of Italian news outlets and an interview study with Italian unions and professional associations. The planned tasks include expert interviews with union and professional association representatives and group interviews with welfare professionals. The postdoc will also support the distribution of a European-wide survey in Italy. A five-page summary of the project plan can be found here. (In the project plan, the position this call relates to is called “PD2”.) Additional tasks within the project may also be allocated to the postdoc that is not mentioned in the project summary, such as organising seminars or workshops and communicating research findings amongst other things. Apart from the tasks appointed to the postdoc in the GIVE RIGHTS project, it is also expected that the postdoc develops one’s own research beyond the immediate needs of the project. In your application, it is important that you both describe how you will be able to conduct the tasks planned for the position in the project and also explain what additional research interests you want to pursue through the duration of the postdoc position – and how these two parts are connected.

review_candidates.description: Nouveau Laboratoire Joseph-Louis Lagrange NICE Alpes-Maritimes Chercheur en contrat CDD 12 mois Doctorat This offer is available in English version Cette offre est ouverte aux personnes disposant d’un titre leur reconnaissant la qualité de travailleur handicapé ou travailleuse handicapée. L'offre en un coup d'oeil L'unité Laboratoire Joseph-Louis Lagrange Type de Contrat Chercheur en contrat CDD Temps de Travail Complet Lieu de Travail 06108 NICE Durée du contrat 12 mois Date d'Embauche 01/12/2026 Rémuneration Entre 3075 euros et 3500 euros bruts mensuels selon expérience Postuler Date limite de candidature : mercredi 28 octobre 2026 23:59 Description du Poste Les Missions Les noyaux galactiques actifs sont un élément clé de l'évolution galactique par rétroaction des AGN sur l’évolution de la galaxie. Ils sont un traceur de la coévolution des trous noirs supermassifs (SMBH) et des galaxies. Ils fournissent des mesures directes de distance géométrique qui devraient pouvoir contribuer au débat sur la tension de Hubble. La spectro astrométrie avec GRAVITY et bientôt ASGARD, sur le VLTI permet de résoudre angulairement la BLR des AGN de type 1, à des échelles inférieures au parsec, et fournit des mesures dynamiques de la masse des SMBH par ajustement de modèle. Combinées aux mesures de taille linéaire par cartographie de réverbération (RM pour Reverberation Mapping), les mesures angulaires par spectro astrométrie fournissent une mesure directe de distance géométrique, parfois appelée « parallaxe BLR ». MATISSE sur le VLTI et le LBTI fournissent des images du tore de poussière et du vent poussiéreux des AGN dans la gamme de 1 à 10 pc. Les estimations de distance de l’AGN et de la masse du trou noir super massif, ainsi que l'étude de la rétroaction des AGN sur la galaxie, nécessitent des modèles et des observations améliorés des AGN à toutes ces échelles, dans une large gamme de bandes et de résolutions spectrales. Les données d'observation de chacune de ces techniques instrumentales sont affectées par des structures qui ne peuvent être analysées avec précision qu'à différentes échelles par les autres instruments. Notre objectif scientifique général est d'étudier les interactions et les contraintes observationnelles mutuelles de la BLR, du tore et du vent de poussière, des flux entrants et sortants et du CND observés par interférométrie différentielle dans les raies d'émission et par interférométrie dans le continu des bandes K, L, M et N, ainsi que les images à plus grande échelle du CND, des flux entrants et sortants et des chocs. Cela améliorera notre compréhension de la rétroaction des AGN, la précision de nos mesures de masse du SMBH et, par conséquent, nos contraintes sur la coévolution SMBH-galaxie. Cela devrait à terme rendre nos mesures de parallaxe du BLR suffisamment précises pour avoir un impact sur le problème de tension de Hubble.
